Take the first laps slow and memorize them, just like you know all the twists and turns on roads you normally take. That's half the battle. Then, you bring up your speed gradually. Pay attention to what gear you're in and what the RPMs are. That's how you measure it.

Never brake in a corner - brake before you get to it. Then, bring up your speed as you exit - being sure to hit the apex. Look where you want to go, not where you're going.

It also helps to "feel" the car. I can tell what the car is doing. I can feel when it's sliding. I can feel when the ass end wants to come around.

Most of the time, your RPMs should be in a fairly similar range - you use the engine and gears to keep it there. You mostly want to be in the lowest possible gear to near redline. The higher gears have less torque immediately available. You can also rotate the car with the gas by causing intentional oversteer. However, that will kill your tires. Managing your tires is important - especially on softer racing compounds. If you don't know what you're doing, you can use your tires up in just a lap or two.
